title: Bounded sixteen-worker configuration and canonical receipt identity
question: Does the compatible pytest/xdist pair run sixteen workers, keep a declared shared group together and preserve native/canonical receipt identities?
method: New bounded sixteen-worker rendezvous and shared-group controls, two actual owned bare native clones, raw report/manifest identity checks; existing successful product cases are not rerun.
commands: uv run python scripts/test_receipts.py run --python-only --out-dir build/test-receipts/qualification/parallel16-compatible-20261106 -- docs/design_review/evidence/2026-11-06_parallel-test-execution/test_parallel_smoke.py -k test_compatible_pair

inputs.role: independent checks of concurrency grouping and canonical receipt identities

outputs.role: unchanged final receipt streams and process artifacts

conclusion: Tested2026-11-06: pytest9.1.1/xdist3.8.0 passed forty newly authored cases, with sixteen actual concurrent workers, one worker for the eight-case shared group, complete provenance for two concurrently owned bare clones, and canonical receipt identities preserving literal parameter @ characters. This is bounded configuration evidence, not full functional or native-capacity qualification. pytest9.2 silently ignored xdist3.8 loadgroup writes; its attempts remain retained and do not qualify grouping.
